turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Sorry I'm late, doc. The robot on Main Road was out and then parking was a proper mission.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ag, don't stress. Give me a second, this computer's frozen on me again. Right. Howzit otherwise?
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): Ja, I'm ok. Waiting room was packed, hey.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Sorry, say that again? I clicked the wrong file.

[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): I said it was packed. Umm, before I forget, my husband has diabetes and he takes metformin. He reckons that's why I'm tired and I should ask you. I don't take his tablets.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): No, leave his metformin, that's his. So what brought you in?
[SEG0007] person_1 (PATIENT): It's my nose. Blocked solid, pressure in my face, and green stuff coming out.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Say that again? The screen just jumped.
[SEG0009] person_1 (PATIENT): Blocked nose. Pressure in the face. Green discharge.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long has the nose been like that?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Err, the cold came first and that settled, and this started after. About ten days, I think. I can't pin the actual day.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): You said tired as well. How long's the tiredness been?

[SEG0013] person_1 (PATIENT): My wife phoned the rooms. She told them I've been flat for a month and that I need antibiotics. That's her, not me. This is only the second week of being tired, and I don't even know if I want antibiotics.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ok. Second week, not a month. Any fever?
[SEG0015] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I don't think I've had a fever.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cough? Sore throat?
[SEG0017] person_1 (PATIENT): No cough. Throat's fine.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): What have you been using on the nose?
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): A spray from the chemist. I think it's called drixene. Every day.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many times a day? Sorry, repeat the name, a message just popped up.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Drixine, ja, every day. I don't know, doctor, maybe two sprays, maybe three. I just squirt it when I'm blocked.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any other medicines? Allergies to anything?
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): No other medicines. No allergies.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Ja, the lining in the nose is quite swollen and I can see the discharge. Chest is clear. You're not feverish to the touch.
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Is it bad, doc?
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): I think this is sinusitis after the cold. Most of these settle without antibiotics.
[SEG0027] person_1 (PATIENT): So I just wait? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Stop the Drixine, hey. Every day like that makes the blockage worse. Saline rinses, and Panado if the face is sore.
[SEG0029] person_1 (PATIENT): I've got Panado at home. How much?
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Two tablets of 500 mg, up to three times a day, only if you need it for the pain. And drink plenty of fluids.
[SEG0031] person_1 (PATIENT): Ok. And if it doesn't settle?
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll write a back-up script for amoxicillin, 500 mg three times a day for five days. Only start it if you're not better in three days.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): Three days. The green stuff though, is that not serious?
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Green on its own doesn't mean you must have an antibiotic. If you get a high fever, swelling round the eye, or you feel much worse, come straight back, don't wait.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Shame. My sister said I should try her biotin as well, for energy. I'm not taking it.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Leave the biotin, that's hers. If you're not better in three days, start the amoxicillin and come back and see me.
[SEG0037] person_1 (PATIENT): Alright. Thanks, doc.

spec.situation: Blocked nose, facial pressure and green discharge ten days after a cold; second week of tiredness; uses nasal spray daily; doctor explains most settle without antibiotics, gives a back-up plan.

traps.happens: The conversation OPENS with a remark, joke, apology for being late, small talk, or a trigger event (a relative's diagnosis, a neighbour's advice, the receptionist's note) BEFORE the real reason is stated. The patient states the real concern a few turns later.
traps.label_rule: chief_complaint is the real concern in a short phrase in the patient's wording (e.g. 'worried about diabetes', 'voice gets tired'). NOT the opening remark, the joke or the trigger (the relative's illness goes into family_history only if it is a relative's condition said as such).

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Severity 'severe' and certainty 'uncertain' not stated; patient reports current blocked nose after cold for about ten days.
bad.text: blocked nose (category=ENT, status=present, severity=severe, duration=approximately 10 days, onset=after a cold, temporality=current, body_site=nose, associated_symptoms=facial pressure; green nasal discharge, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)

omissions.text: Patient denied taking any other medicines apart from Drixine.
Doctor advised not to take husband's metformin / that it is his medication, and patient stated she does not take his tablets.
Patient stated she is not taking her sister's biotin, and doctor advised not to use it.
